requirement_text.REQ-442:
Decision D-A: Mode B (:redirect_single) stays the deployment-wide default; the disclosure mode becomes configurable per tenant with the deployment-wide mode as the fallback; 'uniform' (Mode A) is RECOMMENDED for candidate-facing tenants (for example Bilimbaga exam candidates). Rate limiting stays on in all modes. SIZING ANSWER: this does NOT fit REQ-437's sizing. It needs a schema change on tenants (public schema), a platform-admin write path with authorisation and response-shaping checks, and a change to the lookup query owned by REQ-435, none of which REQ-437 touches; REQ-437 is already one full turn. So it is its own requirement, and REQ-437 consumes its result.
The lookup happens by email BEFORE the tenant is known, so the effective-mode rule is defined over the MATCH SET (ORCH proposal, checked against design s10 and recorded in decision 0043): disclose slug and display name only if there is exactly ONE active match AND that tenant's effective mode is redirect_single; otherwise return the neutral response (and, as before, email the list). A uniform-tenant address is thereby indistinguishable from an unknown one. Checked against the ratified invariants: it does not break the Mode B equivalence class {multi, unknown, malformed, inactive-only, lookup-failure} (it only enlarges it with 'single match in a uniform tenant'), the single-query and no-early-return rules, the constant-work rule (the effective mode is computed in the same query; delivery stays one unconditional off-path submission) or the closed response allowlist; it DOES touch three ratified wordings, flagged below.
BUILDS: 1. A migration adding tenants.login_disclosure_mode (public schema, nullable string, CHECK in ('uniform_plus_email','redirect_single'); NULL = use the deployment-wide default). NOT stored in the tenant :settings blob: that blob has a closed key vocabulary whose values reach the pre-authentication /api/tenant-config and a tenant-admin write path (REQ-382), and the mode is a platform-security attribute that a tenant admin must not set or read. Reversible. 2. The Tenant schema field and a changeset path writable ONLY by PLATFORM_ADMIN through the existing platform-admin tenant update route (locate by grep which route calls Tenant.admin_patch_changeset/2 and extend that path; no new route unless none exists, in which case say so and stop for REQ-VALIDATOR). The change is audited as other platform-admin tenant updates are. A tenant admin's settings route rejects the key (closed vocabulary already does); GET /api/tenant-config and every tenant-admin-readable tenant shape do NOT contain it (INV-2); the platform-admin tenant response may. 3. LOOKUP EXTENSION in Letflow.LoginDirectory (REQ-435): the single query additionally yields, per matched tenant, a boolean disclose computed in SQL: the deployment mode is bound as a parameter; disclose = (deployment mode is redirect_single) AND COALESCE(tenants.login_disclosure_mode, 'redirect_single') = 'redirect_single'. The deployment-wide mode is thereby the fallback (tenant NULL) AND the ceiling (deployment :uniform_plus_email forces every tenant uniform, preserving 0042's configuration-only kill switch). The internal match type becomes %{slug, display_name, disclose}; disclose is consumed by REQ-437's decide/2 and is stripped before any response is built, so the response allowlist is unchanged. Still exactly one query, no tenant :prefix. 4. An unrecognised stored value cannot occur (CHECK); an unrecognised value read in code is treated as uniform.

OPEN QUESTIONS: ["CONFLICTS FLAGGED FOR REVIEWER (decision 0043), not silently resolved: (1) 0042 Standing prohibition 4 and design s5.4 say the lookup returns plain maps with ONLY slug and display_name; this entry adds an internal disclose boolean that never leaves the decision function. (2) 0042 Standing prohibition 11 makes any change to the disclosure shape a security change needing SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off and an amendment to 0042; per-tenant selection is not a third mode but is a new selector, so SECURITY-REVIEWER must sign this entry and decision 0043 D-A is the amending record. (3) Design s7 and 0042 Decision 3 define the mode as a single deployment-wide config; this entry makes it per-tenant with the deployment value as fallback and CEILING. The ceiling is the conservative reading of 'deployment-wide default as fallback' (a tenant can opt into uniform, but cannot opt into disclosure the deployment has switched off); if the BA meant a tenant may also override a uniform deployment default upward, the SQL rule and the kill-switch property change and REVIEWER must decide.", "Who may set it: PLATFORM_ADMIN only is proposed. Whether Bilimbaga (candidate-facing) should be set to uniform_plus_email by a data migration or by an operator action after deploy is an operational choice for ORCH/the operator; this entry ships no tenant-specific data change (decision 0022 bucket rule: nothing here names exams).", "Keycloak Organizations: DEFERRED (BA decision D-G, decision 0043); decide via an ADR when the tenant count grows."]

Must explicitly rule on: (a) ceiling reading of D-A (decision 0043; tenant cannot upward-override a uniform deployment), (b) the 0042 prohibition 4/11 and design s5.4/s7 amendment (needs amending text in decision 0043 / design 434 - say what DOC-UPDATER must write), (c) unaudited-premise correction and the neutral audit action, (d) tenant_map 7th key shared across platform-admin responses, (e) overlap risk with letflow-4 files.
acceptance_criteria: `mix ecto.migrate` and `mix ecto.rollback` both succeed; tenants.login_disclosure_mode exists in the public schema only, is nullable, and the CHECK rejects any value other than the two modes (an insert of 'picker_unauth' fails), real output quoted; existing tenants read NULL

write authorisation: PLATFORM_ADMIN sets the value through the existing platform-admin tenant update route and the change is audited; a TENANT_ADMIN and an ordinary user get the platform's existing refusal; a request body carrying the key to the tenant settings route is rejected by the closed vocabulary; tested through the authorization matrix

no exposure: byte-level assertions that GET /api/tenant-config?realm=<slug> (and the mobile variant) and every tenant-admin-readable tenant/settings response contain no login_disclosure_mode key, for tenants with the value set and unset (INV-2); the platform-admin tenant response is allowed to contain it

lookup matrix, one test per cell, each asserting disclose and exactly one query (telemetry): deployment redirect_single with tenant NULL -> true; deployment redirect_single with tenant redirect_single -> true; deployment redirect_single with tenant uniform_plus_email -> false; deployment uniform_plus_email with tenant NULL or redirect_single or uniform_plus_email -> false (ceiling); an inactive or unbound-realm tenant yields no row whatever its mode

the internal match type carries disclose and no other new field; a test over the lookup function's return and a grep show no login_disclosure_mode, tenant id or idp_realm_id is returned past the lookup; the response allowlist test of REQ-437 passes unmodified
no prefix: the lookup still issues no query carrying a tenant :prefix; log: false on every directory Repo call is preserved

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix test` for the touched areas and `mix letflow.check_boundaries` pass, real output quoted; the SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict is recorded against INV-1, INV-2, INV-5 and INV-6

result.summary: PASS, 0 blockers. Read git diff origin/main...HEAD (lib, priv, test, design). Idiom: no OTP process machinery added; patch_tenant uses cond/with, one Ecto.Multi (update + Audit.append_multi) in a single transaction, fail-closed {:error,:audit_failed}; lookup remains a single prefix-less query with log:false and a bound type(^bool,:boolean) parameter; supervision N/A (REQ-045 plain-context model unchanged, InstanceSupervisor untouched). Scope: no new behaviours, macros or generic plumbing. RULINGS. (a) CEILING reading of D-A RATIFIED: disclose = (deployment == :redirect_single) AND COALESCE(tenant,'redirect_single')='redirect_single'. It is the conservative reading of 'deployment default as fallback', preserves 0042's configuration-only kill switch, and cannot make a tenant more disclosing than the deployment allows. Upward override of a uniform deployment is NOT adopted; if the BA later wants it that is a new decision record. (b) 0042 prohibition 4 (internal disclose boolean) ACCEPTED: 'past the query' is read as 'past decide/2': disclose never reaches a response body, no tenant id/realm id/stored mode leaves LoginDirectory. 0042 prohibition 11 / Decision 3 ACCEPTED as amended by 0043 D-A. DOC-UPDATER MUST WRITE: (1) in decision 0043 add a dated 'REVIEWER ruling (REQ-442)' under conflicts 4-6 stating: ceiling reading ratified; disclose-in-match accepted with the constraint that it is stripped in decide/2 and absent from every response; selector is PLATFORM_ADMIN-only, audited, SECURITY-REVIEWER-signed (INV-1/2/5/6); unrecognised value read in code = uniform. (2) Add 'Amended by 0043 D-A / REQ-442' one-line notes to 0042 Standing prohibitions 4 and 11 and Decision 3 (single deployment-wide mode becomes deployment default AND ceiling plus nullable per-tenant override). (3) In lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login-directory.md amend s5.4 (lookup returns maps with slug, display_name and internal boolean disclose; type tenant_match, tenant_ref retained for reference) and s7 (mode: deployment default and ceiling; decide(mode,result) becomes decide/2 over per-match disclose; s10.2 matrix gains row 'single match in a uniform tenant: 202 neutral, byte-identical to Mode B neutral group'). (4) Update the LoginDirectory/tenants router moduledoc tables if still stale (tenants.ex moduledoc was updated; check README/API docs for tenant_map key list). (c) UNAUDITED-PREMISE correction ACCEPTED: verified patch_tenant and PATCH /tenants/:slug wrote no audit entry and no platform-level sink exists; auditing a mode change in the TARGET tenant's chain, same transaction, is the correct minimal reading of AC2. Action 'tenant.platform_setting.updated' with after_state {changed:true} and nil before_state is neutral and value-free (INV-2). Accepted residual: a tenant admin reading GET /audit can see that some platform setting changed (no name, no value); DOC-UPDATER should record the premise correction in the REQ-442 status event and note display_name-only PATCH stays unaudited. (d) tenant_map 7th key ACCEPTED: tenant_map/1 is private to Routers.Tenants and every route there is :TenantsManage (PLATFORM_ADMIN only); key is present (null when unset) on create/list/get/patch/deactivate/reactivate, which is consistent and allowlist-style. TEST-DESIGNER must assert the 7-key set on every one of those routes (only the get-by-slug test was updated) and that no other shaper (tenant_config, mobile_tenant_config, tenant_settings, onboarding) gains it. (e) letflow-4 overlap: branch feat/REQ-443-pepper-rotation-tooling touches docs/runbooks/login-directory-pepper-rotation.md, lib/letflow/login_directory/key_rotation.ex, two mix tasks and their tests, test/specs/REQ-443.md; NONE of the files changed here (login_directory.ex, identity.ex, tenant.ex, routers/tenants.ex, the migration). Direct conflict risk is nil on committed state; residual semantic risk is that REQ-443/D-C key-id work in login_directory.ex lookup_by_keys would textually collide later, whoever merges second rebases (notably the lookup_by_keys/1,2 arity split). WORTH FLAGGING, non-blocking: (i) TYPE-SAFETY: login_disclosure_mode is :string with the vocabulary duplicated in four places (migration CHECK, Tenant @login_disclosure_modes, router FieldConstraint allowed_values, LoginDirectory string compare). An Ecto.Enum on the field plus router reading Tenant.login_disclosure_modes/0 would make the invalid state unrepresentable; no issue file filed because this gate is read-only on non-handoff files, ORCH/DOC-UPDATER should file a docs/issues entry tagged type-safety. (ii) lookup_by_keys/2 is a public test seam taking the mode as a term; acceptable, but REQ-437 should call /1 only. (iii) deployment_mode/0 duplicates the LoginDiscovery config read to avoid an upward dependency; REQ-437 must keep the two readers in agreement (same key, same nil->redirect_single default, other->uniform). (iv) patch_tenant/2 became /3 with no default; sole caller is the router, fine. Read-only gate: tests were not run.
